key_insight: Agentic RSR connects scene reconstruction, policy learning, and real-robot execution in one task-driven loop. The key idea is to build simulations that preserve what matters for manipulation and to train policies on observations that the real robot can actually use.
problem_solved: Traditional real-to-sim pipelines often reconstruct scenes without considering whether the resulting simulation supports the target task, while policy learning is often done separately from reconstruction. This paper addresses the gap between accurate scene reconstruction and execution-grounded robot control.
method: Start with a workspace video, a task description, and a known robot model.
Reconstruct the scene in simulation with an emphasis on task-relevant objects, interactions, and geometry.
Develop and evaluate policies in the reconstructed simulation using observations aligned with what the real robot will perceive.
Execute the learned policy on the physical robot, closing the real-to-sim-to-real loop through the same manipulation task.
impact: This matters because it makes simulated training more transferable to real robots by aligning reconstruction, perception, and control around the same task. For practitioners, it can reduce sim-to-real mismatch and improve the reliability of robot policies deployed in the real world.
visual_elements: A three-stage pipeline diagram: real video -> reconstructed simulation -> robot execution
A side-by-side comparison showing task-relevant vs. irrelevant scene details in reconstruction
An icon-based workflow linking camera/video, simulator, policy, and robot arm
A success/failure chart illustrating improved transfer from simulation to real execution
paper_title: Agentic RSR: Real-to-Sim-to-Real through Scene Reconstruction and Execution-Grounded Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yihan Li, Yating Feng, Shengjiu Sun, Jianing Chen, Hao Ren
